title: Proper direct image preserves finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, $X,Y$ are separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and $p_X:X\to Y$ is a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^r A=0$ for some $r\ge1$. Work on the small etale sites with constant $A$-coefficients and the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for the full subcategory of $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] consisting of complexes of finite Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

Let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ be a uniform bound for the $\ell$-cohomological dimensions of the geometric fibres: for every geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], every $\ell$-power torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $(X_{\bar y})_{\mathrm{et}}$, where $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-base-change] and $\ell$-power torsion means that every local section of $F$ is killed by some power of $\ell$, and every $i>d$, assume $H^i((X_{\bar y})_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0$, with etale cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For integers $a\le b$ and $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, the total right derived direct image $Rp_{X,*}C$ belongs to $\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d]$.

proof.text: Take the coefficient exponent ell^r. The prime ell is nonzero in the characteristic-p field because p differs from ell. Its power is a unit, and remains a unit after mapping global sections to X and Y. Thus the smooth-base-change coefficient conventions hold on both schemes. Apply the bounded constructible proper-direct-image theorem to C.

For every geometric fibre and every A-module sheaf G on it, its underlying abelian sheaf is killed sectionwise by ell^r: rewrite ell^r times a section as (ell^r times 1_A) acting on that section. Apply the assumed fibre cohomology bound. The module/abelian cohomology comparison and faithfulness of forgetting coefficients give vanishing of module-valued cohomology above d. Global sections over Spec of the algebraically closed field are an exact equivalence. The Leray isomorphism therefore identifies this vanishing with vanishing of the homology sheaves of the fibre derived direct image of G[0].

For a sheaf F on X and q>d, apply proper base change with torsion coefficient ring A to the algebraic-closure point at every point of Y. Finiteness of A gives additive torsion of A. Exact inverse image commutes with homology, and its derived functor takes F[0] to the pulled-back sheaf in degree zero. The bounded-below/total/classical right-derived comparisons identify the pulled-back R^q f_* F with fibre cohomology, which vanishes by the preceding step. Geometric-point inverse images detect zero module sheaves. Hence R^q f_* F=0 for all sheaves F and q>d.

Given any module sheaf M on Y, put B=C tensor^L f^{-1}M[0]. Exact inverse image identifies Lf^*(M[0]) with (f^{-1}M)[0], so the input Tor-amplitude hypothesis puts B in [a,b]. Left t-exactness of right derivation gives Rf_*B in degrees at least a. Apply the proved general derived upper-amplitude theorem to the classical cohomological-dimension bound from the preceding step: Rf_*B lies in degrees at most b+d. This theorem uses dimension shifting on cycles and packages the same finite cohomological-amplitude consequence as the hypercohomology argument.

The finite-coefficient proper projection formula gives (Rf_*C) tensor^L M[0] isomorphic to Rf_*B for every M, with no finiteness or flatness assumption on M. Transport the preceding interval vanishing through this isomorphism to obtain the output Tor-amplitude predicate. Combine it with bounded constructibility from the first step. This tests arbitrary sheaves directly, using the available full relative projection formula, rather than reducing them to constant-module tensors.

proof_origin.place: Constructibility and stalkwise cohomological-dimension argument; uses the full relative proper projection formula (Stacks 0F0G) and the proved general derived upper-amplitude theorem (Stacks 07K7(4)(c)) to test arbitrary sheaves directly.

split_report.statement_dispute: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: without the standing setting, take Y=Spec(k[t_1,t_2,...]), X=Spec(k) defined by I=(t_1,t_2,...), p the closed immersion, and A=F_ell with ell different from char(k). The constant C=A_X[0] has Tor amplitude [0,0], and every geometric fibre has ell-cohomological dimension zero. But p_*A_X has nonconstructible support {I}, since this closed point is not a constructible subset of Y (no finitely many polynomial equations cut it out). Thus the claimed Dctf conclusion fails. The corrected statement explicitly restores the chapter standing setting of sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, already required by lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible, and writes out the etale Dctf notion for arbitrary finite commutative A. No target statement is changed.
